aspects.says: Code you don't control, such as a listener, is called after the lock is released; called under it, it can deadlock in a way the JVM's detector doesn't report.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: a Listener Called Under the Lock
aspects.reason: the deadlock needs a listener that hands work to another thread and waits for it; the seat practice grades the same rule for a slow call, and the page shows the run

aspects.says: A check in one synchronized call and an act in another is not atomic; the decision and the act must happen in one hold of the lock.
basis: section:Each Synchronized Method Is Atomic; a Check Followed by an Act Is Not

aspects.says: In a livelock threads keep reacting to each other without progress, and random back-off breaks it; a monitor makes no fairness promise against starvation.
basis: section:Threads Can Also Stop Making Progress Without Blocking
aspects.reason: livelock shows only under lock-step timing, which the page runs with the module's demo; fairness belongs to ReentrantLock, unit 6.3.1

aspects.says: Two locks taken in opposite orders deadlock; one fixed, unique order used by every piece of code that takes two of the locks prevents it.
basis: section:Two Locks Taken in Opposite Orders Deadlock; One Order for Every Pair Prevents It

aspects.says: notify() wakes one arbitrary waiter, which may not be able to use the change; notifyAll() wakes every waiter to re-check.
basis: section:wait() Belongs in a Loop Over Its Condition, and a Change Is Announced With notifyAll()

aspects.says: With waiters for different conditions on one monitor, notify() can leave a thread waiting although its condition holds.
basis: section:wait() Belongs in a Loop Over Its Condition, and a Change Is Announced With notifyAll()

aspects.says: A monitor other code can reach, such as this, a Class object or a string literal, lets that code stall yours; a private final lock can be taken only by the class.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: Someone Else Holds Your Monitor

aspects.says: A monitor is reentrant: its owner can enter it again, so a synchronized method can call another one on the same object.
basis: section:Each Synchronized Method Is Atomic; a Check Followed by an Act Is Not

aspects.says: The monitor is released however the block exits, and the next thread sees whatever the block wrote before it threw.
basis: section:The Monitor Is Released However the Block Exits, Half-Done Changes Included

aspects.says: synchronized excludes only code that locks the same object; synchronized (new Object()) or an instance lock guarding state shared between instances excludes nothing.
basis: section:synchronized Locks an Object, and Excludes Only Code That Locks the Same One

aspects.says: Slow calls run with no lock held: reserve under the lock, call, then settle under the lock, giving the reservation back if the call fails or throws.
basis: section:Hold the Lock for the State, Not for the Slow Call

aspects.says: A static synchronized method locks the Class object and an instance one locks this, so the two exclude nothing from each other.
basis: section:synchronized Locks an Object, and Excludes Only Code That Locks the Same One

aspects.says: On Java 21 a virtual thread that blocks inside synchronized pins its carrier thread.
aspects.reason: a scheduling property no graded test can observe deterministically; the page shows the trace

aspects.says: A return from wait() doesn't mean the condition holds; wait() is called in a loop that re-checks it.
basis: section:wait() Belongs in a Loop Over Its Condition, and a Change Is Announced With notifyAll()
